Equate the curve and tangent equations:
$$2x^2 + kx + k - 1 = 2x + 3 \implies 2x^2 + (k - 2)x + (k - 4) = 0$$

Apply the tangency condition requiring discriminant $\Delta = 0$:
$$(k - 2)^2 - 4(2)(k - 4) = 0$$
$$(k^2 - 4k + 4) - 8k + 32 = 0 \implies k^2 - 12k + 36 = 0$$

Factorise the perfect square quadratic equation:
$$(k - 6)^2 = 0 \implies k = 6$$

Substitute $k = 2$ into the curve equation and complete the square:
$$y = 2x^2 + 2x + 1 = 2(x^2 + x) + 1 = 2\left[\left(x + \frac{1}{2}\right)^2 - \frac{1}{4}\right] + 1 = 2\left(x + \frac{1}{2}\right)^2 - \frac{1}{2} + 1$$
$$y = 2\left(x + \frac{1}{2}\right)^2 + \frac{1}{2}$$
where $a = \frac{1}{2}$ and $b = \frac{1}{2}$.

State the coordinates of the turning point (vertex):
$$\text{Vertex} = \left(-\frac{1}{2}, \frac{1}{2}\right)$$
